subject.title: feat: sidebar session state slot, worktree/automation badges, archive disables bound cron jobs

question: Should archiving through the existing `sessions.patch` contract implicitly disable bound schedules, or should that durable side effect require explicit caller intent and user confirmation?
rationale: The patch intentionally changes an established RPC action so identical archive requests can permanently mutate admin-owned automation state, and repository policy treats that compatibility and operator behavior as a maintainer product choice.

options.title: Require explicit cascade intent
options.body: Keep archive-only semantics as the default and add an explicit parameter or dedicated action that the Control UI invokes after warning that restore will not re-enable schedules.

options.title: Accept implicit admin cascade
options.body: Retain the current behavior and explicitly accept that admin/internal archive calls silently disable bound schedules until an operator re-enables them.

options.title: Ship indicators without cascade
options.body: Land the session badges and state-slot UI while deferring archive-to-cron mutation to a separately designed workflow.

recommendation.title: Require explicit cascade intent
recommendation.body: Keep archive-only semantics as the default and add an explicit parameter or dedicated action that the Control UI invokes after warning that restore will not re-enable schedules.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent merged history connects this person to both the Control UI archive surface and its localization workflow, and they merged the adjacent session-lifecycle refactor.
